extracted.intended_audience: writers applying for Bread Loaf Writers' Conference financial aid (scholarships and fellowships)
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility rules, selection criteria, and application requirements for Bread Loaf Writers' Conference financial aid (participant scholarships, named scholarships, fellowships, returning awards). Focuses on who may apply, what evidence is required, and how awards are granted/used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for awards: literary merit or published work
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial aid is awarded in recognition of published work or literary promise, and financial need has no bearing on our decisions, except as noted. Awards must be used in the year they are granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection focuses on literary merit or evidence of promise; applicants should understand that need is generally not considered. Award use is limited to the grant year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate application required per financial aid award
rubrics_metrics.description: Each financial aid application requires a separate application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applying for more than one award type (e.g., Participant Scholarship and a Fellowship), submit distinct applications for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship publication restriction (no book in genre)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of those applying for Fellowships, scholarship applicants should not have published a book in the genre in which they are applying nor should they have a book accepted for publication or under contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with a forthcoming book are encouraged to apply for a Fellowship after their book has been published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant Scholarship: emerging-writer focus and review weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Bread Loaf Participant Scholarships are awarded to writers who see themselves as emerging writers ... A record of publication is valued but not required. Though the merit of the manuscript carries the most weight in our application review process, the writer’s responses to the application prompts are also important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant Scholarships cover tuition, room, and board ($4,440). Workshop manuscript merit is primary; application prompts also influence decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant Scholarship: one-time-per-genre rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer may receive a Participant Scholarship only once in a given genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers who previously received a Participant Scholarship in a genre are not eligible for another Participant Scholarship in that same genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant Scholarship: prior Bread Loaf financial-aid ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Former Bread Loafers who received financial aid to attend an in-person August conference are not eligible for the Participant Scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction applies to those who previously attended an in-person August conference with financial aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bread Loaf Katharine Bakeless Nason Participant Scholarship criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Bakeless Participant Scholarships are offered to applicants at the early stages of their writing career whose writing shows exceptional promise ... While literary merit is the main consideration for these awards, writers who meet one or more of the following criteria are encouraged to apply: a member of a historically underrepresented group; an individual who is in particular need of financial and creative support; a first-time Bread Loaf participant; or an applicant with a nontraditional literary or educational background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bakeless Scholarships cover tuition, room, and board ($4,440). Applicants must not have previously received financial aid to attend an in-person August conference. Recipients receive workshop guidance and are invited to read during the Blue Parlor series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bread Loaf–Rona Jaffe Foundation Participant Scholarship criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Bread Loaf-Rona Jaffe Foundation Participant Scholarships are awarded to emerging women writers ... While literary merit is the main consideration, the scholarships are especially intended to support women who have not attended Bread Loaf in the past and also meet one or both of the following criteria: an applicant with a nontraditional literary background ... and/or an individual who is in particular need of financial and creative support. Candidates must be permanent residents of the United States, and writers who have published a book (a standard trade edition of their work) are not eligible for these scholarships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients receive workshop guidance, are invited to read, and the award covers tuition, room, and board ($4,440) plus a $500 travel stipend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning Participant Scholarship eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: Returning Participant Scholarships are available to former Bread Loaf Writers’ Conference Participants who attended in-person within the past five years. This year, those who attended in 2019, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025 are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both former paying participants and former financial aid recipients may apply; applicants are eligible to apply in the same genre that they attended previously. Winners receive workshop guidance, a Blue Parlor reading slot, and the scholarship covers tuition, room, and board ($4,440).

rubrics_metrics.name: Middlebury College Student Participant Scholarship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Middlebury College Student Participant Scholarships are available to current Middlebury College students and also in some cases for recent Middlebury College graduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the conference's Middlebury College Students information for details and any additional eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship publication-eligibility (first or second book within timeframe)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are awarded to applicants who have published their first or second book in English within the last four years in the genre in which they are applying. Writers whose most recent book was published between the years 2022 and 2026 are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are assigned to workshops (often to assist faculty), give a public reading, may submit a proposal for a one-hour craft class, and should note arrival and housing differences (arrive earlier; limited housing; cannot accommodate families). Fellowships cover tuition, room, and board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship: book submission formats and naming requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with the online application, fellowship candidates submit a copy of their book. Applicants should send a Kindle version by going to Amazon.com and choosing Give as a Gift to blwc@middlebury.edu (must be received within 24 hours of the application). If the book is not available via Kindle, upload a PDF or Word file with the application. The electronic file name should have the writer’s last name followed by the book title (e.g., YourLastName__TitleOfYourBook). If unable to send electronically, FOUR copies should be mailed at the time of your application (poetry applicants send THREE copies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Kindle/upload/mail options carefully and adhere to file-naming conventions to ensure your submission is processed. Physical-copy counts differ for prose vs. poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship: book must be in print by conference (galley/proof exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s book must be in print by the time of the conference. If the book isn’t published yet but will be available by August 12, 2026 (the first day of the session), a galley or a proof may be submitted with the application. Please note the publication date on the PDF or Word document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the book will only be available shortly before the conference, include clear publication-date information; acceptance may depend on expected in-print status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellows do not need to submit a manuscript in progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Fellows’ work is not critiqued in workshops or by faculty, there is no need to submit a manuscript in progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship applications should focus on the published book and required copies rather than an in-progress manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning Fellowship eligibility and publication limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: For 2026 Returning Fellowship applicants: recipients who attended in 2024 or earlier and who do not yet have a third book accepted or published are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returning Fellows serve as resources for first-time Fellows and have similar responsibilities (workshop assistance, readings, possible class proposals). Room and board provided for the fellowship recipient only; limited housing prevents accommodating families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning Fellowship: submission logistics (Kindle/upload/mail and copy counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returning Fellowship applications are accepted online and must be submitted by March 15. Along with the online application, fellowship candidates should submit a copy of their book. Send a Kindle version to blwc@middlebury.edu via Amazon Give as a Gift (received within 24 hours), or upload a PDF/Word file. If unable to send electronically, TWO copies should be mailed at the time of your application. For the Returning Fellowship, both poetry and prose applicants send TWO copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the two-copy mailing requirement and electronic submission options; follow the same file-naming conventions as for initial Fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant consideration separate from financial aid decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers who would like to be considered for a spot as a Participant should they not receive a financial aid award must submit a separate Participant Application in addition to the financial aid application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying for financial aid does not automatically enter you for a paid Participant spot; submit the standard Participant Application if you want to be considered regardless of award outcomes.
